prompt: For \(y=2x(5x^3+7/(x+2))\), which simplified formula gives the tangent slope for \(x\ne-2\)?
why: Expand to \(10x^4+14x/(x+2)\). The quotient contributes \([14(x+2)-14x]/(x+2)^2\).

prompt: The function \(y=x^2(3/x^2+4/x^3)\) has slope \(-1\) at which points?
why: For \(x\ne0\), simplify to \(3+4/x\). Solving \(-4/x^2=-1\) gives \(x=\pm2\); use the original height for the coordinates.

prompt: Let \(f(x)=(3x^3-x+2)/x^2\). Which is \(f''(x)\) on the domain of \(f\)?
why: Divide first: \(f=3x-x^{-1}+2x^{-2}\). Differentiate twice to get \(-2x^{-3}+12x^{-4}\) for \(x\ne0\).

prompt: For \(f(x)=(3x^3-x+2)/x^2\), at which point does the graph of \(f'\) have a horizontal tangent?
Which lines are tangent to \(f(x)=x^3-3x^2+2\) with slope \(9\)?
why: Solving \(3x^2-6x=9\) gives \(x=-1,3\). The points are \((-1,-2)\) and \((3,2)\); subtract \(9x\) from each height to get the intercept.

prompt: For \(f(x)=x^3-3x^2+2\), one horizontal tangent is \(y=2\). At which other input does this same line meet the curve, and what is the slope of the curve there?
why: Solve \(f(x)=2\) to get \(x^2(x-3)=0\). The point of tangency is at zero; the other intersection is at \(3\), where \(3x^2-6x=9\).

prompt: For \(f(x)=(x^2+9)/(x^2-1)\), which statement gives all its horizontal tangents?
choices: There are none, since the denominator can vanish.
why: The derivative is \(-20x/(x^2-1)^2\) on \(x\ne\pm1\). Its sole zero is \(0\), and \(f(0)=-9\).

prompt: If \(y=\tan x/(2-\sec x)\), which expression gives \(y'\) wherever the original quotient is defined?
why: The quotient numerator is \((2-\sec x)\sec^2x+\sec x\tan^2x\). Substitute \(\tan^2x=\sec^2x-1\) to cancel both cubic terms.

prompt: For \(f(x)=\tan x/(2-\sec x)\) on \(0<x<2\pi\), how many horizontal tangents does the original graph have?
why: Since \(f'=\sec x(2\sec x-1)/(2-\sec x)^2\), a zero would require \(\sec x=0\) or \(\sec x=1/2\). Neither is possible for a real input.

prompt: Both tangents to \(f(x)=x-4\cos x\) of slope \(3\) on \((0,2\pi)\) have which inputs?
why: Set \(1+4\sin x=3\). On the stated interval the sine is \(1/2\) at \(\pi/6\) and \(5\pi/6\).

prompt: For \(y=2\sin x\cos x\), which equation holds for all \(x\)?
why: The product rule gives \(y'=2\cos^2x-2\sin^2x\). Differentiating again gives \(y''=-8\sin x\cos x=-4y\).

prompt: For \(f(x)=x-4\cos x\), find the tangent line with slope \(3\) at the larger of the two eligible inputs in \((0,2\pi)\).
why: The larger solution of \(\sin x=1/2\) is \(5\pi/6\). Its height is \(5\pi/6+2\sqrt3\); subtract \(3(5\pi/6)\) to get the intercept.

prompt: For \(y=x\sin x\), find the slope of the tangent to the graph of \(y'\) at \(x=\pi/2\).
why: The slope on the derivative graph is \(y''=2\cos x-x\sin x\). Evaluation gives \(-\pi/2\).

prompt: For \(y=\sin x/(1+\cos x)\), which derivative and domain restriction belong together?
why: The quotient numerator is \(\cos x+\cos^2 x+\sin^2 x=1+\cos x\). Cancel one factor wherever the original denominator is nonzero.

prompt: For \(f(x)=x^\pi\pi^x\) with \(x>0\), what is the relative rate of change \(f'(x)/f(x)\)?
why: The first factor contributes \(\pi/x\) after division by \(f\). The exponential factor contributes \(\ln\pi\).

prompt: For \(y=\log_2(6x^4+5)\), find the slope of the tangent at \(x=1\).
why: Change base to \(\ln(6x^4+5)/\ln2\). The chain rule gives \(24x^3/[(6x^4+5)\ln2]\).

prompt: For \(f(x)=e^{\cos x}\), find the slope of the tangent to the graph of \(f'\) at \(x=\pi/2\).
why: Differentiate \(f'=-e^{\cos x}\sin x\) once more. This gives \(f''=e^{\cos x}(\sin^2x-\cos x)\), hence \(f''(\pi/2)=1\).

prompt: The graph \(y=\ln\sqrt{3x-2}\) has a tangent of slope \(1/2\) at which point?
why: On \(x>2/3\), \(y=\tfrac12\ln(3x-2)\) gives \(y'=3/[2(3x-2)]\). Setting this to \(1/2\) gives \(3x-2=3\), so the height is \(\frac12\ln3\).

prompt: For the lecture graph \(f(x)=x^4+3/x\), at which input does the tangent line pass through the origin?
why: The tangent intercept is \(f(x)-xf'(x)\). Since \(f'=4x^3-3/x^2\), its intercept is \(-3x^4+6/x\). Set this to zero and use \(x\ne0\) to obtain \(x^5=2\).

prompt: If \(y=x^3\cot x\), what is the slope of the graph of \(y'\) at \(x=\pi/2\)?
why: First \(y'=3x^2\cot x-x^3\csc^2x\). Differentiating gives \(6x\cot x-6x^2\csc^2x+2x^3\csc^2x\cot x\). Only the middle term survives.

prompt: Which two tangents of slope \(10\) belong to the lecture polynomial \(p(x)=4x^3-2x+7\)?
why: Solving \(12x^2-2=10\) gives \(x=\pm1\). Their heights are \(p(1)=9\), \(p(-1)=5\). Subtracting \(10x\) gives intercepts \(-1,15\).

prompt: For \(f(x)=(x-1)(3x^2+2)\), which slope is the smallest attained by any of its tangent lines?
why: The product rule gives \(f'=3x^2+2+6x(x-1)=9x^2-6x+2\). Completing the square gives \((3x-1)^2+1\), with minimum \(1\) at \(x=1/3\).

prompt: For \(y=\sec x/x\), find the tangent slope at \(x=\pi\).
why: The quotient rule yields \(\sec x(x\tan x-1)/x^2\). At \(\pi\), the secant is \(-1\) and the tangent is zero.

prompt: For \(z=\sin x\tan x\), what is \(z'(\pi/3)\)?
why: The two product-rule terms are \(\cos x\tan x\) and \(\sin x\sec^2x\). At \(\pi/3\) these equal \(\sqrt3/2\) and \(2\sqrt3\).

prompt: For \(f(x)=\ln(2x^3+7)\), at which point does the graph of \(f'\) have a horizontal tangent with positive height?
why: Since \(f'=6x^2/(2x^3+7)\), differentiation gives \(f''=12x(7-x^3)/(2x^3+7)^2\). Of its two zeros, only \(x=\sqrt[3]7\) gives positive \(f'\), and its value there is \(2/\sqrt[3]7\).

prompt: For \(p(x)=4x^3-2x+7\), which term contributes zero to \(p'(x)\)?
why: The derivative of a constant is zero. The two variable terms give \(12x^2\) and \(-2\).

prompt: In the derivative of \(p(x)=4x^3-2x+7\), what does the term \(4x^3\) become?
why: The power rule multiplies the coefficient by \(3\) and reduces the exponent by one.

prompt: For \(p(x)=4x^3-2x+7\), find the slope of the tangent at \(x=-2\).
why: The derivative is \(12x^2-2\). At \(-2\), the squared term is positive and the slope is \(48-2\).

prompt: When applying the product rule to \(x(3-x)\), what is the derivative of the second factor?
why: The constant \(3\) has derivative zero, and \(-x\) has derivative \(-1\).

prompt: Find the tangent slope at \(x=1\) for \(y=(x-1)(3x^2+2)\).
why: The product rule gives \((3x^2+2)+(x-1)6x\). The second term vanishes at \(x=1\), leaving \(5\).

prompt: What is the derivative of \(f(x)=x^4+3/x\) for \(x\ne0\)?
why: Rewrite \(3/x\) as \(3x^{-1}\). Its derivative is \(-3x^{-2}\).

prompt: In radians, what is the derivative of \(3\sin x\)?
why: Keep the constant multiple and use the derivative of sine.

prompt: For \(G(x)=3\sin x-x^2\), what is \(G'(0)\)?
why: Differentiate to get \(G'=3\cos x-2x\), then use \(\cos0=1\).

prompt: What point is on \(y=-2\sin x\) at the input \(x=0\)?
why: Since \(\sin0=0\), the graph passes through the origin.

prompt: Which line is tangent to \(y=-2\sin x\) at \(x=0\)?
why: At zero the height is zero and the slope \(-2\cos0\) is \(-2\).

prompt: If \(y=2x^2-\sec x\), which derivative holds on its domain?
why: Apply the difference rule. The derivative of secant is \(\sec x\tan x\) and the subtraction stays in place.

prompt: For \(z=2\csc x+3/x\), which formula gives \(z'\) on its domain?
why: The derivative of cosecant is \(-\csc x\cot x\). The negative power \(3x^{-1}\) contributes \(-3x^{-2}\).

prompt: For \(f(x)=(x^2+9)/(x^2-1)\), find the tangent at \(x=2\).
For \(f(x)=x^4+3/x\), which input has a horizontal tangent?
why: Multiply \(f'=4x^3-3/x^2=0\) by \(x^2\), valid on the domain. Then \(4x^5=3\) has a unique real solution.

prompt: For \(f(x)=x^4+3/x\), find all points at which the graph of \(f'\) has a horizontal tangent.
why: Set \(f''=12x^2+6/x^3=0\) for \(x\ne0\). Multiplying by \(x^3\) gives \(12x^5+6=0\), with one negative real solution.

prompt: The normal line is perpendicular to the tangent. Find the normal to \(f(x)=3/x^2+1\) at \(x=1\).
why: The point is \((1,4)\) and \(f'(1)=-6\). The negative reciprocal slope is \(1/6\).

prompt: For \(f(x)=3/x^2+1\), find the input at which the tangent is parallel to \(y=3x/4+2\).
why: Equating \(-6/x^3\) to \(3/4\) gives \(x^3=-8\), hence \(x=-2\).

prompt: For \(f(x)=x^3-3x^2+2\), the tangent touches at \(x=a\) and meets the graph again at \(x=4\). If \(a\ne4\), what is \(a\)?
why: Subtract the tangent line from \(f\). The resulting monic cubic has roots \(a,a,4\) because tangency gives a repeated root. Its quadratic coefficient remains \(-3\), so \(2a+4=3\).

prompt: For \(y=x^2(3/x^2+4/x^3)\), at which input is the second derivative \(-1\)?
why: The original domain has \(x\ne0\). Simplifying to \(3+4/x\) gives \(y'=-4/x^2\) and \(y''=8/x^3\). Thus \(x^3=-8\).

prompt: At \(x=0\), what is the second derivative of \(y=2x(5x^3+7/(x+2))\)?
why: Simplify the first derivative to \(40x^3+28/(x+2)^2\). Differentiating again gives \(120x^2-56/(x+2)^3\). Its value at zero is \(-7\).

prompt: For \(f(x)=(3x^3-x+2)/x^2\), what is the nonzero input where the tangent is parallel to the line \(y=3x\)? Write the tangent equation there.

why: Since \(f(1)=0\), this is the product of the two difference quotients at \(1\). Their limits multiply to \(3(-1)\).

prompt: For \(y=2\sin x\cos x\), which inputs in \([0,\pi]\) have tangent slope \(-1\)?
why: Rewrite \(y=\sin(2x)\), so \(y'=2\cos(2x)\). Cosine takes the value \(-1/2\) at \(2\pi/3,4\pi/3\) in a full turn. Halve the angles.

prompt: For \(f(x)=x-4\cos x\) on \([0,2\pi]\), what range of tangent slopes occurs?
why: The derivative is \(1+4\sin x\). On a full turn, sine takes every value between \(-1\) and \(1\).

prompt: For \(f(x)=x-4\cos x\), two parallel tangent lines touch at \(x=\pi/6\) and \(x=5\pi/6\). What is the positive difference between their vertical intercepts?
why: Both slopes equal \(3\). The intercept at \(a\) is \(-2a-4\cos a\). At the given inputs these intercepts are \(-\pi/3-2\sqrt3\) and \(-5\pi/3+2\sqrt3\). The larger minus the smaller is positive.

prompt: For \(f(x)=\sec x/x\) on \(0<x<\pi/2\), which equation characterizes a horizontal tangent?
why: The derivative is \(\sec x(x\tan x-1)/x^2\). Both the secant and denominator are nonzero on this interval.

prompt: For \(z=\sin x\tan x\), simplify \(z'\) entirely in terms of \(\sin x\) and \(\cos x\), on \(\cos x\ne0\).
why: The product rule gives \(\cos x\tan x+\sin x\sec^2x=\sin x+\sin x/\cos^2x\). Bring the terms over a common denominator.

prompt: For \(y=\sec x/x\), what is \(y''(\pi)\)?
why: For \(u=\sec x\), differentiate \(u/x\) twice to get \(u''/x-2u'/x^2+2u/x^3\). At \(\pi\), \(u=-1\), \(u'=0\), and \(u''=\sec x\tan^2x+\sec^3x=-1\).

prompt: For \(G(x)=3\sin x-x^2\), what sign does its tangent slope have at \(x=\pi/3\)?
why: Differentiate to get \(G'=3\cos x-2x\). At \(\pi/3\), cosine is \(1/2\), and \(2\pi/3>2>3/2\).

prompt: For \(f(x)=\tan x/(2-\sec x)\), the original graph has a hole at \(x=\pi/2\). What height and tangent slope would a differentiable filling have there?
choices: No finite height can fill the hole.
why: Near \(\pi/2\), multiply top and bottom by \(\cos x\) to get \(\sin x/(2\cos x-1)\). The denominator there is \(-1\). The quotient rule simplifies its derivative to \((2-\cos x)/(2\cos x-1)^2\), which gives \(2\).

prompt: For \(y=\sin x/(1+\cos x)\), find all points in \((-\pi,\pi)\) at which the graph of \(y'\) has a horizontal tangent.
why: The first derivative simplifies to \(1/(1+\cos x)\). The second derivative is \(\sin x/(1+\cos x)^2\), zero only at \(0\) in the interval. The requested height is \(y'(0)=1/2\).

prompt: For \(y=x\sin x\), where do the tangent lines at \(x=\pi/2\) and \(x=\pi\) intersect?
why: The derivative is \(\sin x+x\cos x\). At \(\pi/2\) the slope is \(1\) and the height is \(\pi/2\), giving \(y=x\). At \(\pi\) the slope is \(-\pi\) and the height is zero. Solve \(x=-\pi(x-\pi)\).
